_comment: THE MUTANTS, COMMITTED, because the alternative is grading my own homework.
An author-written mutant list contains the mutations the author's tests
already catch. On 2026-09-28 one scored 18/18 on this package while an
independent sweep found ten survivors. A list a reviewer can read is the part
that makes the score mean anything -- what is checked, and what is not.
Add a mutant whenever a defect reaches main: the mutation is the proof the
new test would have caught it. The Python SDK carries the same file, and the
two should stay comparable -- this is one command with two implementations.
Each entry replaces `find` with `replace` in `file`, once, then runs the
suite. A SURVIVOR is a change to production code that breaks nothing.

mutants.name: finish() swallows the write error
mutants.why: Node hands end's callback the stream error. Discarding it made ENOSPC print 'done: N rows', record complete, and exit 0 with a truncated file.

mutants.name: no 'error' listener at stream creation
mutants.why: write() never throws synchronously, so a filesystem error becomes an unhandled 'error' event that kills the run with five of six parks unattempted.

mutants.name: a resumed failure deletes the accumulated file
mutants.why: `written` counts rows THIS process wrote; on a resumed run the file holds everything earlier runs fetched.

mutants.name: the empty-window skip deletes a resumed file and exits 0
mutants.why: A key rotated out of a cron's environment wiped the partial archive and exited 0, so the scheduler logged success.

mutants.name: the column fingerprint is ignored
mutants.why: A file written under a different header resumes and gains rows no reader can parse.

mutants.name: a state file from the other SDK is accepted
mutants.why: The two SDKs' keys differ only on the interrupted path, so the safe paths interoperate silently and a cross-SDK resume duplicated 64 of 108 rows.

mutants.name: the checkpoint comes from the newest row
mutants.find: const nextFrom = page.next === null ? null : nextPageFrom(page.next);
mutants.why: An entity that stopped reporting has no rows for the tail days of its page, so resuming there re-downloads days already written.

mutants.name: csvCell stops quoting a carriage return
mutants.why: One row parses as two, with every later column shifted.

mutants.name: the CSV loses its BOM
mutants.why: Excel on Windows reads the local code page and mangles every registered mark and accent.

mutants.name: a negative number is prefixed as a formula
mutants.why: Every negative value in the file becomes text and arithmetic breaks in the tool the prefixing protects.

mutants.name: a query that folds to empty matches everything
mutants.why: normalize('東京') is '', and ''.includes is true of every string, so a CJK query listed all 127 parks as candidates.

mutants.name: the ambiguity list sorts by uuid
mutants.why: Sorting the formatted line sorts by the id it starts with, so ten Hurricane Harbor parks came back in an order that looks random.

mutants.name: a bare --list is an error again
mutants.why: parseArgs makes the value mandatory, so `--list` exited 2 while the help advertised `--list [TEXT]`.

mutants.name: --list swallows the next flag as its filter
mutants.find:
const next = argv[i + 1];
  return next !== undefined && !next.startsWith('-');
mutants.replace:
const next = argv[i + 1];
  return next !== undefined;
mutants.why: `--list --out x` would filter on '--out' and list nothing.

mutants.name: an empty API key counts as a key
mutants.why: THEMEPARKS_API_KEY="" is a clobbered env var in a cron file, and the anonymous notice never printed.

mutants.name: no positionals costs a request
mutants.why: Running with no arguments fetched /destinations first, so with no network it exited 75 -- telling a scheduler to retry a command that can never succeed.

mutants.name: --version drops the command name
mutants.why: A bare 8.3.0 cannot be pasted into a bug report, and the Python SDK prints the name.

mutants.name: the page hook fires before its rows
mutants.why: A consumer that died mid-page would record a checkpoint past rows it never wrote. Losing rows is worse than duplicating them.

mutants.name: a daily row loses the name the response gave it
mutants.find: for (const row of entity.days) yield { entityId: entity.id, ...label, row };
mutants.replace: for (const row of entity.days) yield { entityId: entity.id, row };
mutants.why: The name a row is labelled with must be the one recorded then; a park's current children list rewrites history for a ride since renamed.

mutants.name: the generated columns drift from the contract
mutants.why: This SDK wrote 32 columns while Python wrote 41. The shared csv_contract.json fixture is what stops the two diverging again.

mutants.name: a finished park is never fetched again
mutants.why: A rerun printed 'already complete' and exited 0 without asking for a new day, so a nightly cron looked healthy and never updated.

mutants.name: the run ends at retrievableThrough
mutants.why: retrievableThrough is usually today. Ending there wrote the day so far, and the unsettled days before it, as if they were final.

mutants.name: --since is ignored on a first run
mutants.why: The flag parsed but the download still started at the top of the archive.

mutants.name: an earlier --since than the file is accepted
mutants.find: if (since !== null && askedFrom !== null && since < askedFrom) {
mutants.why: Appending cannot add days before the file's first one, so accepting it hands back a file that is not what was asked for.

mutants.name: a --since past the file's end leaves a gap
mutants.why: Starting after the day the file continues from leaves a gap the state file cannot describe.

mutants.name: a fixed --since before the key's floor is refused the next night
mutants.why: On a plan short of the archive the file starts at the key's first day, so judging --since against that refused the same cron line the next night.

mutants.name: --since after --until is accepted
mutants.why: A range that can never be satisfied should be refused before any request is spent on it.

mutants.name: a day that does not exist is accepted
mutants.why: Date rolls 2025-02-30 over to March 2; the person did not ask for March.

mutants.name: a finished file with a foreign layout is appended to
mutants.why: Only an unfinished mismatched state was refused; a finished one got the whole archive appended under a second header, exit 0.

mutants.name: a state without its data file is continued
mutants.why: Continuing writes a file that starts part-way through its range and records it as complete.

mutants.name: no checkpoint before the first request
mutants.why: A run killed before its first page left no state, or an extending run's state still said complete; the next run started over or skipped the days.

mutants.name: an 8.3 file keeps its partial tail
mutants.why: 8.3 wrote the newest days while they were still changing and never replaced them.

mutants.name: the trim ends a CSV record at a quoted newline
mutants.why: A name with a line break in it is one record, not two; splitting it corrupts the kept rows.

mutants.name: an anonymous 8.3 file is trimmed to nothing
mutants.why: A file wholly inside the cut would be emptied and continued from a day the key can no longer read.

mutants.name: a continued file jumps forward to the key's floor
mutants.why: Carrying on from the key's first day instead of the file's next day leaves a gap the file then claims not to have.

mutants.name: changeRows drops opening
mutants.why: Without the opening, the time before an entity's first change has no known status: 63 seconds of Space Mountain on 2026-09-26.

mutants.name: load() and iteration make two requests
mutants.why: Reading opening must cost the same single request the rows do.

mutants.name: finalThrough is the later of the two days
mutants.why: The later day is retrievableThrough on most keys: today, whose row is not final.

mutants.name: onPage is not awaited
mutants.why: The next page was requested while the checkpoint was still being written, so a kill in between recorded the wrong page.

mutants.name: a resume does not cut back to the checkpoint
mutants.why: Rows written after the last checkpoint by an interrupted page were kept, and the resume appended the same page again.

mutants.name: a checkpoint does not wait for the rows
mutants.why: The size recorded would not cover the rows before it, and the resume would cut some of them off.

mutants.name: overlapping runs are not locked out
mutants.why: Two runs appending to one file interleave rows and each records its own checkpoint.
